correctness.rationale: For Hardy H² Szego kernels, F_mu(re^{iθ})=(1-r²)/(A-B e^{iθ}), A=1-(1-mu)r² and B=mu r³, traces a complete circle with real center c_r and radius rho_r. Direct algebra gives a_mu<c_r<1 and rho_r/(1-c_r)=r/(1+mu r²)<1/(1+mu), so every circular section lies strictly inside the convex hull of 1 and the limiting circle center a_mu=1/(2+mu), radius a_mu. Conversely r->1 supplies that circle, while w=0 supplies 1; hence the entire closed convex hull is exact. Compactness of the radial parameter excludes interior tangent segments from the closure of the actual Berezin range. Tangent-disk geometry yields the stated area and the identity-endpoint jump, d_H(K_mu,{1})=1 as mu->0+. Independent finite checks of 25 radii and sampled boundary points confirmed the strict supporting inequality; the analytic proof handles the continuum 0<mu<1.
residual_risks: The result is about the closed convex HULL, not a classification of every point in the nonconvex Berezin range; mu=0 excluded from positive-parameter hull formula.
